items.evidence: horizon-items/src/items.rs LootContext::modifiers() (line 2401) covers 11 of the 19 function kinds 26.2's data uses; the default arm _ => {} (line 2607) silently no-ops copy_components, furnace_smelt, set_enchantments, set_stew_effect, set_name, exploration_map, set_ominous_bottle_amplifier, set_instrument. expand() (line 2227) has no minecraft:tag arm (default _ => false, line 2319). Counted over all 1,355 tables: 102 carry >=1 unhandled function/entry — 71 block tables (copy_components), 18 entity (furnace_smelt 16, set_ominous_bottle_amplifier 1, tag entry in entities/creeper.json), 9 chest, 3 equipment, 1 archaeology. Survival gameplay is largely shielded: block breaking is covered by game/spill.rs Pending::record/attach (lines 44/100), which copies block-entity components by BE type and covers all six distinct include sets in the data (34x custom_name-only, 17x shulker set, 16x banner set, 2x bees, 1x pot_decorations, 1x skull set); only lock/container_loot on shulker boxes are not copied (unreachable in vanilla survival). Entity/chest/fishing loot goes through loot.rs in gameplay, which handles every kind those tables use. What breaks is /loot (cmd_loot, terrain_cmds.rs:585), which routes every table through items.rs: /loot mine on a shulker box drops it empty, /loot kill on a creeper loses the music-disc tag entry, /loot kill on a cow loses furnace_smelt, /loot on chest tables loses set_name/set_enchantments/set_instrument/set_ominous_bottle_amplifier/set_stew_effect/exploration_map. Condition handling is complete (all 12 kinds), so only functions/entries are affected.

items.evidence: crafting.rs Ingredient::parse_object (line 123) requires a neoforge:ingredient_type or type key and returns None otherwise, so vanilla object forms ({"item": "..."}, {"tag": "..."}) fail to parse and the recipe is dropped. No vanilla 26.2 recipe uses object ingredients (all 3,542 ingredient slots are strings, plus 84 array slots whose elements are all strings), so this affects only player datapack / mod recipes using the object form. Same code and same data property as 1.21.7's B12-G05.

systemic_note: The prepared data is faithful — all 5,516 data-driven files byte-identical to the 26.2 jar, block-tags.json byte-faithful too. The 1.21.7 systemic finding (code reading the 26.x form of formats the version writes differently) does NOT carry to 26.2: 26.2 writes the OLD form — its loot JSONs use the condition/function discriminators and plural conditions arrays (the type rename is a 26.3 change), its specials are already data-driven, and its effect table legitimately has 40 entries. What remains is narrower: items.rs is a block-drop engine with a partial loot-function set, reused by /loot for every table type, so command-rolled tables silently lose the functions and entry types it never implemented (B12-G01).
